title: Redwood February 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership gave a company update: healthy topline growth, cautious runway extension, product focus on Optimize and Private deployments, Dedicated capacity improvements, and hiring priorities. Q&A covered benchmarks, compliance timeline for Private, and customer wins. Clear next steps around pricing refresh, security pack share, and a follow-up metrics deck.
transcript:
Header: 2026-02-11 09:00 PST | Duration: 63 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Laura, Miguel, Priya, Ravi, Kelsey + all staff (virtual)

[00:00] Laura: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're a little light on slides today but wanted to do a straight update and leave lots of time for q and a. Quick shout out to the eng and infra teams for the Dedicated rollout last month — big ops win.
[00:28] Miguel: Yeah I'll just kick off with a few infra notes, we saw a 12% improvement in p99 token latency on our standard workload after the kernel selector changes, that was from the feb patch. There's still some noise in the multi-tenant traces where the KV cash — sorry KV cache — warms slowly for very short sequences, we're looking at caching heuristics to avoid regression for chat-like workloads.
[01:03] Priya: On product, Optimize is shipping beta to a handful of customers next week. The big win is automated batching suggestions and a new quantization recommendation flow; early internal tests show 35-45% cost per token reduction on embedding-heavy workloads. Note: numbers vary by model and seq length.
[01:38] Ravi: Eng update — throughput projects are ahead of plan, but we still need more headcount in performance teams. We're planning two more senior infra hires and a TPM to help with Dedicated autoscaling policies.
[02:12] Kelsey: Finance/ops, quick note on runway — we're tracking slightly ahead of plan on ARR, but churn in a few mid-market accounts tightened short-term cash. We've extended our runway target to 22 months assuming modest hiring pace.
[02:45] Audience (chat): Congrats on the benchmarks!
[03:05] Laura: Thank you. Customer wins — shout out to FinEdge and Graphly for committed Dedicated contracts. These wins validate both the economics and compliance angle for enterprise customers.
[03:30] Miguel: A technical note on Private deployments: we've completed the VPC control-plane MVP for two partners, but we still need to finish the KMS/HSM integrations and SOC 2 evidence collection. Expect formal SOC 2 package by end of Q2.
[04:00] Priya: Roadmap highlights — next 90 days: 1) Optimize beta, 2) Dedicated autoscale improvements, 3) Private: KMS + audit logs, 4) Console UX polish for routing and rollouts.
[04:35] Speaker 1: Are we prioritizing latency or cost for the hosted API customers?
[04:45] Miguel: Good q. It's contextual: PLG tier stays latency-first with lower batch sizes; the paid tiers can opt into more aggressive batching/quant params. We want sensible defaults but give customers explicit knobs.
[05:15] Audience (mic): Any updates on model catalog—support for new open models?
[05:25] Priya: We're adding two community models next month and updating performance profiles in the catalog. Also improving streaming and function-calling consistency.
[05:50] Laura: Hiring — we still need to slow hiring in non-core functions but double down on infra, security, and solutions engineering. Recruiting sheet link in the follow up.
[06:12] Miguel: Benchmarks — internal perf spreadsheet referenced, note that some of our earlier numbers had measurement flukes on 1k token tests, fixed those and updated results. We will circulate a public benchmark doc for customers next week.
[06:40] Audience (chat): Security pack? When will we get the security docs?
[06:48] Kelsey: We'll share the security pack (SOC2 + infra diagrams + SSO docs) by Feb 18.
[07:00] Q&A starts, various questions about pricing, private deployment timelines, and dedicated SLA.
[07:30] Audience (mic): For Private customers, what's the timeline for HSM / bring-your-own-key?
[07:40] Miguel: We're targeting BYOK + HSM support in early Q3; some partners will be on a pilot earlier.
[08:05] Audience: How do we compare to competition on cost?
[08:12] Priya: We position as cost-efficient for production inference with transparent tradeoffs; we call out per-route economics in the console so customers can choose. Competitors like Anthropic/OpenAI/AWS Bedrock come up in sales, but our differentiation is serving and economics.
[09:00] Laura: OK quick recap — wins: Dedicated deals, latency improvements; work in progress: Private SOC2/KMS, Optimize beta; risks: churn in a few mid-market accounts and hiring pace.
[09:25] Laura: Next steps — we'll send out the metrics deck, security pack, and a calendar invite for a deeper private deployment technical deep dive next Tuesday.
[09:40] Audience: Thanks!
[09:45] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript has occasional mishears (KV cash) and speaker attribution may be generic; chat reactions not fully captured.

Ravi: Open reqs for 2 senior infra hires and a TPM; have job postings live by 2026-02-20
